The core mathematical structure revolves around establishing a bijective mapping between body poses and spatial locations within bounding boxes. When this mapping fails—specifically, when multiple poses are mapped to a single location—an error condition emerges. This is modeled as a failure of injectivity in a function f: P → L where P represents body poses and L represents locations. The dual nature of the problem lies in both the presence of missing or erroneous data and the need for resolution mechanisms. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian inference over uncertain pose-location pairs, while in GSE, it translates into state transitions guided by minimal-distance heuristics. The failure mode occurs when the cardinality constraint |P| ≤ |L| is violated, leading to ambiguity. Resolution involves either eliminating redundant poses or selecting the most probable match based on geometric proximity. The derived kernel of this structure is the error function E(pose, location) = ||pose_centroid - location||, minimized over possible pose assignments.
